text:
Ava: Heading on a 5am redeye tomorrow. Need two things: a playlist that will make me sob quietly at 30,000ft, and a book that's small but emotionally big. GO.
Marco: Holocene by Bon Iver on repeat for the crying part. For a tiny book that punches above its weight: The Art of Racing in the Rain — airport tissues recommended. :tissue_box:
Priya: If you want cinematic sobs, add 'On the Nature of Daylight' (Max Richter) — instrumental that hits like a freight train. For a short but heavy read, try "The Sense of an Ending" (Julian Barnes).
Ethan: I threw together a quiet redeye playlist — 'overnight-quiet-sob' (public-ish): https://open.spotify.com/playlist/37i9dQZF1DX6ziVCJnEm59?si=placeholder  — tracks: Bon Iver • Agnes Obel • Max Richter • Sufjan Stevens.
Sara: Audiobook rec if you want to fall asleep and wake up somewhere else emotionally: 'Klara and the Sun' narrated by Sinead Matthews — very soft delivery. @Ava might like that during takeoff.
Ava: Ooh, love Sufjan. Does anyone have a single-track tearjerker rec? Trying not to make my seatmate uncomfortable.
Marco: Single track = 'The Curse' by Josh Ritter or 'Lua' by Bright Eyes for whisper-cry vibes.
Priya: 'The Night We Met' (Lord Huron) will absolutely do it. Also, pro tip: put on noise-cancelling + low volume so it feels private.
Ethan: tiny playlist snippet (copy/paste into your player):
```
1. Bon Iver — Holocene
2. Max Richter — On The Nature Of Daylight
3. Sufjan Stevens — Fourth of July
4. Agnes Obel — Riverside
5. Lord Huron — The Night We Met
```
Sara: For a short book that still wrecks you: 'The Sense of an Ending' already suggested — or 'We Have Always Lived in the Castle' if you want eerie instead of sad.
Ava: Paperback or audiobook for flying — opinions?
Marco: Paperback if you actually want to re-read lines. Audiobook if you want to nap and be led into crying. :sleeping:
Priya: Paperback for planes with good overhead light, otherwise audiobook. Also bring hand sanitizer wipes.
ops-bot: FYI Ava — gate change alert: now departing from B12, boarding 04:30.
Ethan: If anyone wants the full playlist file, I can export a .m3u or drop a direct Spotify share. Quick LMK.
Sara: Thanks for all recs y'all. My redeye reading pile just got very emotional. :sob: :coffee:
